review_comment: I remember in the old days we couldn't catch this and expect the JVM to really be in a working state. Has that changed?

I'm not sure what the exact concern was. One of the challenges with Errors (e.g. OOM) being thrown is that they can just happen anywhere in the code, and if the surrounding exception handling logic isn't handling and dealing with arbitrary Throwables, it can leave the program in an odd state (resources not being cleaned up etc). I'm not aware that it would do something bad with the JVM or bring it to an undefined state (but happy to learn more about that if it were the case). I therefore think that it's not a concern for Lucene's Regexp class, which isn't holding onto any resources or requires any kind of special clean-up. Maybe @rjernst has more thoughts on this?
The Lucene regex class is indeed fairly contained. If there's any place safe to catch this then I think this is one of them.

I talked with @ChrisHegarty about this. He [linked](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/master/src/java.base/share/classes/java/util/regex/Pattern.java#L1441) me to where the jdk does this when *it* compiles regexes. I'd say we're in good company then.
But interestingly they don't propagate the whole overflowed stack when they rethrow, so I think it's worth making the change I suggested in my other comment.
